title: Front-line Transparency: Public Safety Organisations in Romania Expand Body Camera Fleet to Protect Officers and Increase Transparency
summary: Front-line Transparency: Public Safety Organisations in Romania Expand Body Camera Fleet to Protect Officers and Increase Transparency
body_markdown:
- Establishes a framework agreement with Motorola Solutions enabling the Romanian Police and other public safety organisations to expand their existing body camera fleet.
- Built upon an existing base of more than 23,000 Motorola Solutions body cameras actively deployed and trusted across Romanian public safety agencies.
- Provides up to 20,000 additional VB400 body cameras nationwide.


Across Europe, front-line officers operate under heavy strain, balancing high call volumes and unpredictable encounters with a growing administrative burden. When an incident escalates, officers must make fast, high-stakes decisions with little room for error. Without clear video footage to document what actually happened, routine encounters can dissolve into protracted disputes and contested complaints.


**Expanding Frontline Transparency Nationwide**


To address these growing operational demands and strengthen public trust, Romanian public safety organisations are undertaking a comprehensive modernization of their front-line police technology. Building on more than 23,000 Motorola Solutions body cameras already deployed and proven across agencies - including the Police, Border Police, Gendarmerie and Prison Administration - public safety organisations are further expanding their video security fleet.


The Romanian Police recently signed a new framework agreement with[Motorola Solutions](http://www.motorolasolutions.com/) to deploy up to 20,000 additional[VB400 body cameras](https://www.motorolasolutions.com/en_xu/video-security-access-control/body-worn-cameras/vb400.html) nationwide. While the Police serves as the central contracting authority, the framework is structured to allow all Romanian public safety organisations to expand their fleets. This initiative broadens the technology’s coverage across urban, rural, and border jurisdictions to help ensure a larger proportion of front-line officers carry reliable recording capabilities on every shift.


**Engineering Reliable Hardware and Integrated Software Workflows**


Deploying technology to tens of thousands of officers across diverse geographic regions presents substantial challenges. Hardware carried on duty must withstand extreme weather, physical impacts, and high-stress encounters without failing or adding unnecessary weight to an officer's tactical vest. Simultaneously, the underlying digital evidence software must process and secure video footage easily as part of existing workflows.


The VB400 body camera was engineered specifically to meet these operational demands, featuring:


- Rugged exterior enclosure
- Full-shift battery operation lasting up to 12 hours
- Wide-angle lens that captures essential contextual details during incidents


When officers return to precinct stations at the end of a shift, docking the unit initiates automatic footage uploads directly into[VideoManager software](https://www.motorolasolutions.com/en_xu/video-security-access-control/videomanager.html) . The system automatically tags video files with time, date, GPS location and associated incident case numbers, maintaining an unbroken chain of custody.


Ken Fiddes, sales director for International Mobile Video Solutions at Motorola Solutions, said:


*"Our engineering team focused on ensuring that advanced recording technology never distracts an officer from their primary responsibility of maintaining public safety. By pairing rugged VB400 hardware with VideoManager software, we built a seamless digital solution that simplifies evidence processing from the moment a recording starts in the field to its final review in court."*


**Proven Operational Outcomes**


Field experience with more than 23,000 body cameras in daily service across Romania demonstrates strong user satisfaction and clear operational impact. On the front line, visible recording consistently helps deter hostile behavior and de-escalate volatile encounters. Behind the scenes, tight integration between the cameras, VideoManager and existing police IT infrastructure is cutting down the time required for digital evidence processing and court preparation.


**Establishing Resilient Foundations for Future Safety Innovations**


As public safety requirements grow more complex across Europe, the integration of video security, digital evidence management and mission-critical communications will remain central to modern policing strategies. Expanding body camera capabilities provides Romanian law enforcement with a resilient technological foundation capable of incorporating future software enhancements and data analytics.


Martin Fuerst, MSSSI vice president for Central and Eastern Europe at Motorola Solutions, said:


*"Motorola Solutions has worked closely with first responders in Romania for more than two decades to help them transform public safety. By expanding their fleet of VB400 body cameras, the Romanian Police continue to lead public safety modernization in Eastern Europe, and we remain committed to supporting their mission to build safer communities."*
